title: Singaporeans Earning $1,300 or Less a Month on Take-home Basis
what_it_is: Singaporeans Earning $1,300 or Less a Month on Take-home Basis

sections.label: Low-wage employees and self-employed
sections.summary: About 30,000 full-time Singaporean employees and 22,000 self-employed persons receive under $1,300 monthly, including Workfare and CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Including Workfare and CPF contributions, there are about 30,000 full-time employees among Singaporeans receiving less than $1,300 per month; likewise, for 22,000 self-employed persons.

sections.label: Workfare disbursements and recipients
sections.summary: From 2007 to 2019, over $6.8 billion went to 890,000 lower wage workers, with about 400,000 receiving Workfare yearly in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From 2007 to 2019, over $6.8 billion has been disbursed to 890,000 unique lower wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In the past three years, an average of about 400,000 individuals receive Workfare annually.

sections.label: Average and maximum Workfare payouts
sections.summary: Over the same period, the average annual Workfare payout was about $1,560, while the maximum was $3,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: During the same period, the average Workfare payout received annually was about $1,560, while the maximum was $3,600.

sections.label: Profile of 30,000 low-wage workers
sections.summary: The 30,000 employees include clerks, F&B workers, cleaners and salespersons; many have lower education, and over a third are aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: On the Member's question about the profile of the 30,000 workers, among the 30,000 employees are office clerks, F&B workers, cleaners, shop salespersons as well as several other smaller groups of occupations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Many of them have lower education profiles, of which four in five have post-Secondary qualifications and below, while half of them have Secondary education and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: More than third of them are aged 50 and above, which reflects an older profile who have less access to higher education as compared to the current generation.

sections.label: Household income of low-wage employees
sections.summary: Half of the 30,000 full-time Singaporean employees live in households with per capita income above $1,300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Out of this group of 30,000 full-time Singaporean employees, half of them live in households with household income per capita above $1,300.

sections.label: Workers' Party minimum wage proposal
sections.summary: The Workers' Party manifesto 2020 calls for all working Singaporeans to receive a minimum take-home wage of $1,300 monthly for full-time work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: According to the Workers' Party manifesto 2020, it calls for all working Singaporeans to receive a minimum take-home wage of $1,300 per month for full-time work and pro-rated for part-time work.

sections.label: Minimum Wage level clarification
sections.summary: A Member is asked to clarify the Minimum Wage level the Workers' Party proposes, given ILO earnings definitions and conventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If this is the case, then the gross wage inclusive of CPF contributions should be higher – between $1,600 and $1,700, thereabouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Given the statements put out recently and in line with ILO's definition of earnings to include contributions to social security and international conventions of Minimum Wage to be before tax deductions and social security contributions, could I ask the Member to clarify what is the Minimum Wage level that the Workers' Party is proposing.

sections.label: Reason for $1,300 raise
sections.summary: The $1,300 figure was raised partly because it reflected a reasonable basket of goods and services for adequate living in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In part, the reason why we raised $1,300 was because that was the notion of how much a reasonable basket of goods and services for adequate living in Singapore would entail.

sections.label: WIS payout adjustments
sections.summary: WIS payouts were significantly adjusted across age bands, with a 45-year-old's maximum payout about $2,500, more than double 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Since WIS was first introduced, we have made significant adjustments to the payout quantums across all age bands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With the WIS Enhancement recently done – just made in January this year – the maximum WIS payout would be, for a 45-year-old, for example, about $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This is more than double the payout of such workers in 2007 when we first introduced WIS.

sections.label: Workfare motivating seniors to work
sections.summary: The pre-2020 maximum of about $3,000-plus, roughly 30% of an older worker's salary, motivated some seniors to work or continue working.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: I am glad the Member noted that the maximum amount that we had given before 2020 was about $3,000-plus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: That translates to about 30% or one-third of an older worker's salary, which studies have shown, has motivated some of our seniors to go back to work or continue working because they get the extra boost from Workfare to supplement their incomes.
